newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 2.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Wednesday:
- A school principal has been suspended pending an inquiry into allegations that one of his sons sat a Leaving Certificate examination on behalf of his brother.
- The government is coming under pressure to widen the scope of a payments-to-politicians tribunal to let it investigate the purpose of a secret bank accounts containing up to 40 million pounds.

- Health minister Brian Cowen was defiant last night as he faced a wave of criticism of his decision to rescind 24 appointments to health boards made by his predecessor in the government ousted in June 6 elections.

- The government has been presented with an awkward political problem for its first Dail sittings next week with the opposition demanding an extension of the terms of reference of the payments-to-politicians inquiry.
- Thousands of people turned up to watch a spectacular fireworks display over Victoria harbour yesterday evening to celebrate Hong Kong's unification with China.
- Prime Minister Bertie Ahern is to raise his concern about this weekend's disputed Drumcree march in Northern Ireland at a meeting with British Prime Minister Tony Blair on Thursday.
- Politicians dropped from health boards by Helath Minister Brian Cowen within hours of taking up their appointments warned last night that they would take legal action to reverse the decision.
- A solicitor's plans to give his bride the honeymoon of a lifetime turned into a South Pacific nightmare. The pair were awarded 10,235 damages by a Dublin court on Tuesday.
